newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones index edges up but stalls again at 6,000.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones index edges up but stalls again at 6,000.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average held a modest gain Tuesday after stalling once again in its attack on the 6,000-point level.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow was up 10.06 points at 5,989.87 following 30-point rally to 6,010.37.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances by a small margin on volume of 260 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"The assault on 6,000 is not over," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "But some undercurrents of profit-taking, while not overbearing, are keeping the market in check."
The Nasdaq Composite index was off 2.01 at 1,248.86 and the American Stock Exchange index lost 1.44 at 580.78.

Early in the session, bullish comments about the semiconductor industry from Merrill Lynch analyst Thomas Kurlack helped fuel a rally in technology stocks, among them bellwether Intel Corp., which hit an all-time high.

Later in the session, however, Salomon Brothers downgraded Intel's shares, citing the company's high stock price as one reason for the move. Intel, which hit 107 at its peak, eventually slipped 3/8 to 104-1/4.
The debate over Intel mirrored a broader one taking place on Wall Street that has seen some analysts turn cautious over the course of the market's recent rally.
"Personally, I don't think we're going to close over 6,000 today," said Peter Green, vice president of technical research at Gruntal & Co. "I'm getting a little cautious on a short-term basis here."
Even analysts who expect the market to continue higher in the very short term said the Dow would likely remain stuck under the milestone 6,000 level for a number of sessions.
"We'll hem and haw here a little bit," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "But this move is not yet complete."
Bleier predicted the Dow would hit 6,200 before undergoing any meaningful retrenchment.
In individual issues, McDermott International Inc. fell 2-1/2 to 19-1/2 after announcing a larger loss in the latest quarter and was slashing its quarterly dividend by 80 percent.
American Brands Inc. jumped 3-5/8 to 48-1/8 as investors cheered a plan to spin off the company's British-based Gallaher tobacco business.
Expeditors International of Washington Inc. surged 5-1/4 to 40-1/2 after the company said its third quarter earnings per share could be up by as much as 50 percent from a year-ago.
